claim: Cueing a memory during sleep raises later recall by a small amount: Hedges g=0.29 [0.21,0.38] over 91 experiments, N=2004 (re-checked in the paper).
agent_test: Cue-and-replay step vs no replay at equal tokens; expect a small gain.

claim: The pooled TMR effect shrinks under publication-bias correction: three-parameter model g=0.13 [0.06,0.21], trim-and-fill g=0.18; severe one-tailed scenario gives g=-0.05. Published vs unpublished did not differ significantly (Q(1)=1.005, p=.316). No pooled update after 2020 was found (PubMed scan).
agent_test: Plan for true effects near 0.1-0.2; use paired tests with many items.

claim: The effect depends on sleep state: NREM cueing works (SWS g=0.27, N2 g=0.32); REM (g=-0.06) and wake (g=0.07) do not pool to an effect (stage Q(4)=10.74, p=.030). Gap search: REM can impair (Yuksel 2025) and mouse SWS vs non-SWS NREM flips the sign.
agent_test: Run replay only in an isolated consolidation state with no fresh input; compare the same pass done in-task at equal tokens.

claim: Fear and conditioning TMR is unclear: human conditioning g=-0.03 [-0.35,0.29] (4 experiments, N=91), SCR g=-0.08; mouse NREM cueing weakened fear; odor-context extinction (Hauner 2013) was positive. Gap search: mouse sign depends on substage (NS cueing weakened, SWS cueing strengthened fear, Zheng 2024); humans: positive result for PTSD therapy cue (n=17 vs 16) and for weakening via interfering positive memory.
agent_test: No LLM analogue; skip.

claim: Skill and procedural learning show larger pooled gains than declarative (skill g=0.44 vs declarative g=0.23), but single studies vary (Rasch 2007 finger tapping null, g=-0.08).
agent_test: Test cue-replay on procedure-like tasks (multi-step recipes) vs facts.

claim: Cue modality matters little: auditory verbal 0.26, nonverbal 0.23, olfactory 0.32 (Q(2)=0.69, p=.709).
agent_test: For an LLM, cue form is a prompt choice; test cue types empirically.

claim: Recall and performance outcomes show TMR; recognition (g=0.18, CI crosses 0), SCR and subjective ratings do not.
agent_test: Score the agent on free recall, not multiple-choice recognition.

claim: Founding result: odor cue at learning and again in SWS improved spatial card-pair recall (g=0.69 [0.19,1.18], N=18); REM odor cueing (N=17, g=-0.05) and awake cueing had no effect.
agent_test: Background; no direct test.

claim: Sound cues for individual items in NREM improve item-specific memory within person (25 cued vs 25 uncued objects; 1.07 vs 1.23 cm error, N=12; Hu 2020 table gives g=0.48, p=.095, for this study).
agent_test: Replay chosen items only and compare with unreplayed items inside one run.

claim: Benefit is largest for weakly learned items; near-ceiling items gain nothing; strengthening encoding did not rescue awake TMR. Gap search: two 2026 studies find only encoding-strength-dependent effects; but phonotactically difficult words got no benefit at all (eLife 2024, N=22), so very weak traces may not be rescued.
agent_test: Replay only items the agent got wrong or is unsure of; compare with replaying everything.

claim: Adapting cue dosage to item difficulty helped the hardest items (personalized beat TMR t22=3.96); groups of 12, one lab, two reports of the same dataset. Gap search: now peer-reviewed (NPJ Sci Learn 2025) but still one lab; a difficulty counter-result exists.
agent_test: Allocate replay count by item difficulty vs fixed count at equal tokens.

claim: Cue count does not predict gain; sleep physiology does (SWS time, spindles). Cue-number correlation rho=0.02 in one study.
agent_test: Gate replay on a state check, not on number of repetitions.

claim: Awake TMR is mostly null or harmful: a 14-result table is mostly null, and Hoffman 2024 (N=40,40,41) found disruption in Exp 1 and no effect in Exps 2-3.
agent_test: Check that re-presenting cues mid-task hurts vs replay in a separate pass.

claim: TMR replicates poorly in recent work: SWS vs N2 (N=34) no overall cued benefit; SleepStim home TMR (N=61) no overall effect; face-name (N=24) null overall; theta-tACS plus TMR (N=37) null; cueing 1x vs 5x (N=31) null; odor TMR 2026 (N=32) null overall. Gap search: further nulls 2024-2026 (odour-cued set N=32, word-meaning priming, once vs five cues N=31, odour plus sound).
agent_test: Expect fragile gains; run many items and seeds and report null results.

claim: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation raised oscillations but not memory in two replications (N=12, N=19); this is not item-specific TMR but shows an oscillation change is not sufficient.
agent_test: Do not accept an internal proxy as proof of better answers; measure outcomes.

claim: Up-state timing may matter: closed-loop cues at slow-oscillation up states improved recall (N=16); home closed-loop vocabulary TMR cued +8.6% vs uncued -4.6% (N=24). Small samples.
agent_test: Timing analogue is replay when context is quiet; weak support.

claim: Cueing is not holistic: it can sharpen distinguishing features and hurt shared ones; a CLS model predicts costs to non-targeted memories when the store is plastic. Gap search: replaying a competing memory weakens an older one (PNAS 2024), stacked odour cues cancel benefit (2026), and week-old memories resisted harm.
agent_test: Measure accuracy on non-replayed neighbouring items after a replay pass.

claim: Emotional and valence effects are mixed: negative items gained in RT not accuracy (N=15); NREM cueing helped emotional items only (N=62); REM cueing of emotional items impaired (2025).
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM.

claim: Replaying a sound attached to counter-stereotype training reduced cued implicit bias (N=40, built-in replication; 1-week F(1,37)=4.67).
agent_test: Analogue: replay of a debiasing rule attached to a cue; low priority.

claim: No study was found that tests TMR (an external cue biasing which memory is replayed) on a language model. Re-checked 2026-11-19: none of 49 citers of Sleep-time Compute tests a cue-triggered replay by title.
agent_test: Build it: a cue token tied to a stored lesson, re-presented in an isolated replay pass, vs uncued lessons.

claim: Offline pre-computation helps LLMs: sleep-time compute cut test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy, up to +13% (GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (AIME) when scaled (abstract re-checked); wins at low budgets, loses at high; benefit tracks query predictability. Gap search: IdleSpec re-ran it in tool agents and found it at or below vanilla in some settings; benefit tracks predictability and many reuses.
agent_test: Do an offline pass over context before questions; compare at equal total tokens (sleep plus test).

claim: Sleep-style consolidation for LLM weights (Behrouz 2026): Qwen3-8B AIME-24 79.2 vs GRPO 76.4, OPSD 76.6, SFT 75.5; removing Dreaming drops knowledge incorporation from 48.1 to 35.7. Needs weight updates, not a scaffold.
agent_test: Out of scaffold scope; motivation for a rehearsal pass only.

claim: Looped offline passes help: more recurrent sleep passes raised cellular-automata exact accuracy from about 10% to over 30%.
agent_test: Fast-weight method; not scaffold.

claim: Gated memory maintenance helps small models under interference: SleepGate 99.5% at depth 5; decay-only was no better than baselines; SCM 22/22 with 24 items vs FIFO 8/22. Tiny models and 22 questions.
agent_test: Compare gated eviction vs FIFO on a long-context agent.

claim: Sleep-inspired replay in neural networks helps continual learning and calibration: WSCL ablation 4.70 to 35.68 with NREM plus REM; SRC ECE 0.0622 to 0.0130.
agent_test: Mixed old/new rehearsal pass vs none in a continual-learning setting; not LLM-specific.

claim: Replay is causal in rodents and CLS models: V1 engram inhibition in sleep disrupted fear memory; the model gain lasts only if the hippocampal store consolidates its own replay.
agent_test: Theory only.

claim: Idle-time pre-computation helps when the next need is predictable and the cost is reused, and fades or hurts when observations are uncertain: IdleSpec re-ran Sleep-time Compute (Qwen3.5-4B 33.2 vanilla to 29.4; Gemini-2.5-Flash 50.5 to 50.1) while its conditional planning gained 5-7 points; ProAct (predictable need chains) cut turns 14.8%.
agent_test: Compare pre-computed notes for the predicted next step vs conditional plans, at equal idle tokens, with predictable and unpredictable follow-ups.

claim: Extra offline study budget does not reliably raise performance: flat from $1 to $50 on two of three benchmarks; one rose 0.271 to 0.348. Studied artifacts cut the test-time rollouts needed (2 to 8 rollouts for no-study to match).
agent_test: Cap idle passes; test study spend vs extra test-time samples at equal total cost.

claim: Offline consolidation passes need a cadence: Auto-Dreamer did best at k=10 on ScienceWorld, worse at k=1 and k=20; no seed variance reported.
agent_test: Sweep pass frequency at fixed token cost.

claim: An LLM agent that rewrites its memory each night from the day's transcript keeps cross-session recall (71+-7 vs 0 with no rewrite); distorted replay does not improve transfer and wrong-detail distortion cuts recall (76 to 60 at 40%).
agent_test: Replay must be faithful; do not add noise as regularisation.

claim: No pooled TMR meta-analysis newer than Hu 2020 was found; 2024-2026 single studies are mixed (at least five nulls or encoding-strength-only effects against six positives, most with N 16-80), so plan for g about 0.13-0.29.
agent_test: Use paired designs with many items; treat small effects as the baseline.

claim: TMR can change the sign of a memory's fate by what is replayed with the cue: a suppress-instruction tone increased forgetting, a competing positive memory weakened an aversive one, and extra odour cues cancelled the benefit.
agent_test: Replay an item together with a tag (keep or drop) and a rival; check neighbours.
